sources.title: RFC 5545 — Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar)
sources.locator: §3.2.19 TZID; §3.3.5 DATE-TIME; §3.8.2.4 DTSTART; §3.8.3.1 TZID; §3.8.4.4 RECURRENCE-ID; §3.8.4.7 UID; §3.8.5.1 EXDATE; §3.8.5.3 RRULE; §3.8.7.4 SEQUENCE
sources.observed_operation: Read the normative recurrence, identifier, time-zone, exception and revision sections; no implementation was executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A local DATE-TIME without TZID is floating; fixed local times use UTC or local time with time-zone reference. Each TZID used requires a matching VTIMEZONE with valid coverage for every recurrence. RECURRENCE-ID names the original occurrence start. EXDATE excludes values from the recurrence set. UID is persistent and globally unique. SEQUENCE is initialized at 0 and monotonically increments on significant revisions when used.
sources.applicability: Normative iCalendar semantics for the proposed feed and optional .ics snapshot; does not establish that any named commercial client implements every recurrence feature identically.

sources.title: Subscribe to someone else’s calendar — Google Calendar Help
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Google Calendar Help content accessed 2026-10-10; Google Calendar SaaS build/release not exposed.
sources.locator: § Use a link to add a public calendar; lines 54–61 in retrieved page
sources.observed_operation: Observed official steps: computer browser → Other calendars → Add other calendars → From URL → paste published calendar URL → Add calendar.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A link can be added only if the calendar is public. New URL subscriptions are set up on a computer browser; the same Help page says the mobile Google Calendar apps do not support subscribing to a new calendar.
sources.applicability: Google Calendar's documented public-feed subscription flow, not a promise about all Google client versions or refresh cadence.

sources.observed_operation: Read official instructions for public link and public iCal address.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The public iCal address works only if calendar is public. Google says removing public access usually takes a few minutes but may take up to four hours. Calendar event defaults can themselves be public unless changed.
sources.applicability: Disclosure review for the proposed Google route. This supports treating public calendar content as publicly accessible, not as member-only.

sources.title: Import or subscribe to a calendar in Outlook.com or Outlook on the web — Microsoft Support
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Outlook.com support content accessed 2026-10-10; consumer service build not exposed. The page labels the article Applies To Outlook.com and has separate Outlook-on-the-web/work-school guidance later in the article.
sources.locator: Consumer Outlook.com section: Subscribe to a calendar, Upload a calendar from a file, and difference between importing and subscribing; lines 119–191
sources.observed_operation: Observed official consumer route: sign in on web → Calendar → Add calendar → Subscribe from web → URL → Import. Also read Upload from file route.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Online subscription refreshes automatically, usually approximately every three hours but can take more than 24 hours. Uploading an .ics file is a snapshot and never refreshes the imported events. The separate work/school part of the page gives different cadence text and is out of the selected consumer scope.
sources.applicability: Only the documented Outlook.com consumer web operation and cadence. Does not establish desktop Outlook, all Outlook-on-the-web tenants, or third-party client cadence.

sources.observed_operation: Read official URL-subscription setup flows on iPhone/iPad and Mac.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For the subscription to appear across the user’s devices, Apple says to sign in with the same Apple Account and choose iCloud as the account/location in the documented flows. No refresh interval is stated.

sources.title: RFC 4791 — Calendaring Extensions to WebDAV (CalDAV)
sources.released_version_or_commit: RFC 4791, Standards Track, March 2007; updated by RFC 5689, 6638, 6764, 7809, 7953 and 8996 per RFC Editor metadata.
sources.observed_operation: Read the standard's definition of calendar-aware WebDAV access and its calendar object/collection model.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CalDAV is a calendar access protocol over WebDAV and iCalendar calendar objects, requiring a server implementing the calendar-access feature; it is distinct from downloading one static .ics resource.
sources.applicability: Standards-level analogy for a more capable server-sync design. No deployment or selected commercial CalDAV server was tested.

sources.title: RFC 6578 — Collection Synchronization for Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV)
sources.locator: Abstract; §3 synchronization-token overview; `sync-collection` operation and example reports
sources.observed_operation: Read protocol definition and token-based routine synchronization example.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Client presents a previous sync token; server returns changed, added or deleted collection resources and a new token. First synchronization requests a full listing. It requires compatible WebDAV server and client support.
sources.applicability: Explains the distinction between change-aware server synchronization and periodic `.ics` feed polling.

sources.title: dateutil issue #614 — TZID is not supported in rrule DTSTART
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2018-01-18; milestone 2.7.0; later closed through PR #624.
sources.locator: Description and issue metadata; example is `DTSTART;TZID=America/New_York:20180119T130000Z`
sources.observed_operation: Read issue report and linked resolution history.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The parser reportedly rejected the TZID parameter. The reporter's example combines TZID with a Z-suffixed UTC value, which RFC 5545 forbids; use a local DATE-TIME without Z for a standards-conforming test.
sources.applicability: Historical issue context for the dateutil parser only; explicitly not evidence of a Google/Microsoft/Apple defect.
